Can you redesign just one screen?

Do I get the design files?
Premium includes design files and a short style guide. Smaller packages include mockups of the new screens, and the final result lives in your code.
desc:
iOS app redesign and UI refresh gives your existing iPhone app a modern, consistent interface without touching your users or their data. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your flows, shares new designs for approval and rebuilds the screens in SwiftUI or UIKit.

## What is an iOS app redesign?

An iOS app redesign is a new visual and interaction design for an app that already works. Colors, typography, spacing, icons, navigation and screen layouts change. Accounts, features and stored data stay where they are.

The work has two halves. The first is design: how each screen should look and behave. The second is rebuilding those screens in code, so the new interface is real and testable, not just a picture.

## Why an interface ages

Apps pick up clutter over time. Each new feature adds a button, a menu or a tab, and nobody removes the old ones. Visual styles drift as different people add screens. Apple also changes its design language, and an app that ignores it begins to feel out of place next to the apps around it.

Users read this as quality. An interface that looks dated or inconsistent suggests that the product is neglected, and people hesitate to trust it with payments or personal information.

## How a redesign affects usage and perception

A clear interface lowers the effort of every task. When buttons look like buttons, text is easy to read and the main action is obvious, people finish what they came to do. Fewer wrong taps and fewer abandoned screens follow from that.

Perception matters as well. Screenshots on the App Store are your first impression, and a tidy modern interface makes the page more convincing. A redesign cannot fix a weak product, but it removes a barrier between a good product and the people judging it.

## What a good redesign includes

- A review of current flows to find where people hesitate or get lost.
- New colors, type and spacing, defined once and reused everywhere.
- Reusable components, such as buttons, cards and input fields.
- Mockups for approval before any code is written.
- Navigation that is simpler to understand, with fewer levels.
- Dark mode support, so the app looks right in both appearances.
- Accessible text sizes and contrast.
- Smooth, restrained animations and transitions.
- Design files and a short style guide at handover, in the larger package.

## How we work

We begin by using your app and listing the screens people see most. Then we propose a direction: palette, type and a few key screens as mockups. You approve or adjust the direction before we rebuild anything.

Once approved, we rebuild the screens one by one in SwiftUI or UIKit, depending on what your project uses, and connect them to your existing logic. Basic refreshes up to three screens and the icon. Standard covers the main flows with reusable components and dark mode. Premium covers a complete redesign with simplified navigation, an accessibility pass and polished transitions.

Your users update the app as usual. They keep their accounts, their data and their settings.

## Redesign without rewriting

A visual refresh does not need a rewrite of the app's logic. We change the interface layer and leave networking, storage and business rules alone wherever possible. That keeps risk low and the project quick to test. If a screen cannot be restyled cleanly because its code is tangled, we tell you before we start and suggest a sensible fix.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Name the three screens that matter most to your users.
- Share your brand colors, logo and any style rules.
- Give feedback on mockups in writing, screen by screen.
- Follow Apple's design guidance for navigation and controls.
- Test the new look with a few real users before release.

**Avoid:**
- Changing everything at once if users rely on familiar habits.
- Using trendy effects that hurt readability.
- Low-contrast text on colored backgrounds.
- Moving core features to unexpected places.
- Skipping dark mode and larger text checks.

## Who this is for

This suits an owner whose app works well but looks older than competitors. It also suits a company that has just updated its brand and needs the app to match, and a team that has added features for years and wants order restored. If you only need one problem screen fixed, a small package is enough.

## What we need from you

Share the source code through a collaborator invitation, or at least a build and screenshots, along with brand files and examples of designs you like. For the release build, a limited team role in App Store Connect is enough. We never need your passwords. After you order, we send a short questionnaire, then the first mockups.
